title: Parameter of the sum of two independent Poissons
source: Theory S2-3.4 Quick check 1 (8); lambda plus mu
stem: \(X\sim\operatorname{Po}({lam|int})\) and \(Y\sim\operatorname{Po}({mu|int})\) are independent. Write down the parameter of the distribution of \(X+Y\).

steps.name: A
steps.note: A is lam+mu. Original 3 and 5 give 8.

title: Scaling a Poisson rate to a shorter interval
source: Theory S2-3.4 Quick check 2 (2); constant-rate scaling
stem: The number of events in a 5-minute period has the distribution \(\operatorname{Po}({p|int})\). Write down the parameter of the distribution for a 1-minute period, using the same model with a constant rate.

steps.name: A
steps.note: A is 2k. Original k=1 gives Po(10) in 5 minutes and parameter 2 in 1 minute.

title: Total of two independent Poissons on a 2-minute period

source.note: 9709/72/M/J/11 Question 5(i) only [3]. Official QP and official MS. Part (ii) omitted.

stem:
This question is 9709/72/M/J/11 Question 5(i) only, taken from the official QP.

The number of adult customers arriving in a shop during a 5-minute period is modelled by a random variable with distribution Po(6). The number of child customers arriving in the same shop during a 10-minute period is modelled by an independent random variable with distribution Po(4.5).

(i) Find the probability that during a randomly chosen 2-minute period, the total number of adult and child customers who arrive in the shop is less than 3. [3]

steps.name: B
steps.note: Official MS: B1, Po(3.3) seen or implied. Independent: adults in 2 min Po(2.4), children in 2 min Po(0.9), total Po(3.3).

steps.name: M
steps.note: Official MS: M1, Poisson P(0)+P(1)+P(2). Allow +P(3). Allow a wrong parameter. Accept an equivalent method.

steps.name: A
steps.note: Official MS: A1, 0.359. Independent: exp(-3.3) times (1 + 3.3 + 3.3 squared over 2) = 0.35894... = 0.359.

contexts.note: Stem taken from the official QP PDF, Question 5(i) only. Official MS reproduced mark by mark. Paper already used Q3(i) in S2-2.1; Q5 is free. Paper/self-mark.
